latest.title: Will AWS Emulator Replace the AWS Blocks Mocks? What Running Both Revealed About a Third Testing Layer
latest.description: AWS Emulator reproduces AWS APIs locally, while AWS Blocks ships its own local mocks. The two replace AWS at different layers: Blocks swaps in mocks at import time, and the emulator answers SDK calls. Running the same operations against both in CI, KVStore matched the mock, and FileBucket returned the S3 behavior that DESIGN.md only describes in prose. IAM and PostgreSQL remain gaps. A contributor's reading of why the emulator fits as a third layer between the mocks and the sandbox.

trending.title: Can AI agents escape a Lambda MicroVM sandbox? Strands Box prevented it.
trending.description: AI agents are starting to act outside the lines they are given, so I tested the worst case: I put one in a Lambda MicroVM and told it to escape, with 13 techniques from current security research. The microVM boundary held the flag, the credentials and the control plane on its own, but the agent still tunnelled data out over DNS. A Strands-Box-style policy stopped that too, blocking 44 of 49 moves and cutting sensitive exposure from 9 kinds to 0.
